To add on to what @shiny said, you can think of the difference as a wall. Opacity will make you lose the ability to see the wall, meaning that you won't be able to see the texture, the color, or even border the wall has. Background color, on the other hand, only changes the color of the wall. You can make it red, blue, or even see-through, like glass, but the borders and textures can still be there if you want to.

The only difference is that IIRC opacity is more widely supported than rgba().

I recommend using something like this for a fallback

background-color: #FFFFFF; /*or whatever colour you want*/
background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0);
